The market punishes uncertainty over risks.

It’s often better to fully realize a risk than to have it pending.

When risks are uncertain, modeling their impact on an asset is theoretically open-ended, which means an asset can potentially be worth nothing and can’t be properly hedged either.

Realizing a risk brings clarity, leading to more accurate and truthful modeling. It also allows for a shift in the narrative.

In essence, the best bottoms are formed against the prevailing consensus, often in times of deep fear or anxiety, following a significant positive price reaction to the worst news.

At the same time, hedge funds purchased +$1.2 billion, bringing their 4-week average of purchases up to +$1.6 billion.

Meanwhile, retail investors sold -$2.2 billion last week, posting their 8th consecutive weekly sale.

Retail investors have now sold an average of -$1.9 billion in US equities per week over the last 4 weeks.

Institutions are buying while retail is selling.

At the same time, Manufacturing PMI surged +3.1 points, to 57.0, its highest since May 2022.

Excluding the # pandemic reopening surge in demand, the latest improvement in business activity is the strongest since 2015.

However, this growth comes amid severe supply chain bottlenecks and labor shortages, pushing backlogs sharply higher and adding to inflationary pressures.

China’s oil imports from Iran are collapsing:

China imported ~6.9 million barrels of crude oil per day in the first 20 days of September, near its lowest level in 10 years.

This is well below the ~10.5 million barrels per day China imported on average before the Iran War.

At the same time, Chinese imports of Iranian crude dropped to ~80,000 barrels per day, on track for the # level in at least 10 years.

This is down -92% to -95% from the 1.0 to 1.5 million barrels per day imported before the war.

As a result, China has imported ~600 million fewer barrels of seaborne oil this year than it would have if it had maintained 2025 import levels.

China is also partially replacing Iranian crude
